title: Explain the effect of outliers on summary statistics
show: dot plot of 12,14,15,17,18,19,45 with 45 far from the rest

example.question: Seven students recorded the minutes they spent on homework: $12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 45$. The value $45$ is removed. Find how much the mean falls and how much the median falls. Which one is affected more by the outlier, and why?

steps.say: Add all seven values and divide by $7$. With seven values the median is the 4th one.

rows.aside: The middle (4th) value is $17$, so the median is $17$.

steps.say: Now there are six values. Add them and divide by $6$. The median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th values.
Subtract each new value from the old one. The mean fell by $\hl{1}{\frac{25}{6}}$ and the median fell by $\hl{2}{1}$.
Say it in words. The mean uses the total, and $45$ is a big part of that total. The median only uses the middle position.

rows.aside: The mean changes a lot because the outlier is added into the total. The median changes little because it depends only on the middle values, not on how large the biggest one is.

title: Analyse plots to explain differences in centre and spread
show: two box plots for Class A and Class B on one scale

example.question: Two classes sat the same test. Five scores are taken from each. Class A: $10, 12, 13, 14, 16$. Class B: $8, 12, 14, 16, 20$. Find the mean and standard deviation of each class and compare the two classes.

steps.say: Add the scores and divide by $5$ for each class.
Standard deviation: square each distance from the mean, average them, then take the square root.
Do the same for Class B, using its mean of $14$.
Say which centre is higher and which spread is larger, with the numbers.

rows.aside: Class B has the higher mean ($14$ against $13$), so it did slightly better on average.
Class B also has the larger standard deviation ($4$ against $2$), so its scores are more spread out. Class A is more consistent.

title: Interpret a histogram in terms of distribution
show: histogram of homework times with the class widths and frequency heights

example.question:
The histogram shows the time, in minutes, that 60 students spent on homework one night. The classes and the number of students in each are: 0–20: 5; 20–40: 22; 40–60: 8; 60–80: 4; 80–100: 21.
(i) Describe the shape of the histogram.
(ii) Estimate the mean.
(iii) What does the histogram tell you about the students?

steps.say: Look for where the bars are tallest. Name each peak and say how many students it holds.

rows.aside: The bars between the peaks are short. The shape is **bimodal**: it has two peaks.

steps.say: Use the middle of each class as its value. Multiply by the number of students, add, and divide by the total.
A mean is only an average. Check how many students are really near it.

rows.aside: The mean $\hl{1}{54.7}$ minutes is in the class 40–60.
Only 8 of the 60 students are in that class.

steps.say: Say what the shape means for the students, in the words of the question.

rows.aside: There are two groups: students who worked for about half an hour and students who worked for about an hour and a half. Hardly any student worked for the mean time of $\hl{1}{54.7}$ minutes, so the mean hides the two groups.

title: Use the sampling distribution of the mean
show: normal curve for the sample mean, narrower than for single bags, centred at 500

example.question: The weight of a bag of flour is normally distributed with mean $500$ g and standard deviation $12$ g. A sample of $36$ bags is taken. Find the probability that the mean weight of the sample is greater than $503$ g.

steps.say: The sample mean has the same mean, $500$. Its spread is the standard error: divide $\sigma$ by $\sqrt{n}$.
Turn $503$ into a $z$-score. Use the standard error as the spread.
The tables give the area to the left of $z$. We want the area to the right, so take it from $1$.

title: Construct a 95% confidence interval for a proportion
show: number line with the sample proportion and the 95% confidence interval either side

example.question: In a random sample of $500$ voters, $120$ say they will vote for a new candidate. Find a $95\%$ confidence interval for the proportion of all voters who will vote for her. Give the limits to $4$ decimal places.

steps.say: The sample proportion is the number who said yes, divided by the sample size.
The margin of error is $1.96$ times the standard error. Put $\hl{1}{0.24}$ and $n = 500$ into the formula.
Subtract $\hl{2}{E}$ for the lower limit and add it for the upper limit.

rows.aside: State it as an interval: $0.2026 \le p \le 0.2774$.

title: Perform a two-tailed z-test of a population mean
show: normal curve for the null mean with the rejection region tails shaded and the sample mean marked

example.question: A machine is set to fill bags with a mean of $250$ g. The standard deviation is $6$ g. A sample of $36$ bags has a mean of $247.9$ g. Test, at the $5\%$ level of significance, whether the mean fill has changed. State your hypotheses and your conclusion.

steps.say: The null hypothesis says nothing has changed. The alternative says the mean is different, in either direction.

rows.aside: $H_1$: the mean fill is not $250$ g.

steps.say: Subtract the claimed mean from $\bar{x}$. Divide by the standard error, $\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}$.
At the $5\%$ level, the limits are $-1.96$ and $1.96$. Is $\hl{1}{z}$ outside them?

rows.aside: $-2.1$ is less than $-1.96$, so $z$ is in the rejection zone.

steps.say: Say what it means for the machine, not just for $H_0$.

rows.aside: Reject $H_0$. There is evidence that the mean fill of the machine has changed.
